rationale: C03 is a strong drafting-template candidate. It predates the child by eight months, concerns delegation of presidential authority within the Department of Defense, and uses the same distinctive operative formula: the Secretary of Defense together with subordinate military-department secretaries designated by that Secretary may act “without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President.” The child materially adapts this machinery into separate provisions for the Army, Navy, and Air Force academy authorities. C19 and C16 share the general enumerated-delegation form and close language, but neither matches the child’s Defense Department hierarchy and repeated service-secretary structure as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense, and, when designated by the Secretary of Defense for such purpose, the Secretary of the Army are hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense, and, as designated by the said Secretary for this purpose, any of the Secretaries, Under Secretaries, and Assistant Secretaries of the military departments, are hereby designated and empowered to perform the following-described functions of the President without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim delegation formula combining the Secretary of Defense, subordinate officers selected by that Secretary, and authority exercisable without further presidential action.

shared_material.child_excerpt: SEC. 2. The Secretary of Defense, and, when designated by the Secretary of Defense for such purpose, the Secretary of the Navy ... SEC. 3. The Secretary of Defense, and, when designated by the Secretary of Defense for such purpose, the Secretary of the Air Force
shared_material.parent_excerpt: SECTION 1. The Secretary of Defense, and, as designated by the said Secretary for this purpose, any of the Secretaries ... of the military departments ... SEC. 2. The Secretary of Defense, and, as designated by the said Secretary for this purpose, the Deputy Secretary of Defense and any of the Assistant Secretaries of Defense
shared_material.explanation: The child expands C03’s hierarchical Defense Department delegation structure into parallel service-specific sections for the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the authority vested in the President by [specified act and citation] ... to designate persons who may be permitted to receive instruction
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The authority vested in the President by [specified act and citation] to [perform the delegated function]
shared_material.explanation: Both orders implement the delegation through an enumerated sequence of statutory authorities, each identified by enactment and codified citation and followed by a concrete description of the transferred presidential function.
